findings.title: Postgres skip added — hides eager-init regression
BuildIndex no longer serializes per key — duplicate indexes possible
findings.body:
The previous version held `b.cacheMu` for the entire BuildIndex call, so concurrent calls for the same key were serialized and the cached index was consistent. The new version only locks when assigning `b.cache[key] = idx`. Two concurrent calls to `BuildIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` (for example, two simultaneous `Search` requests that both find the cache empty via `getOrCreateIndex`, or the init goroutine racing with an incoming search) will both:
  1. Open separate bleve indexes (file or memory),
  2. Run the builder to write all documents,
  3. Flush,
  4. Race to write `b.cache[key]` — last writer wins, the loser's index is orphaned in memory and the work is wasted.
The PR description frames this as "finer grain locking", but the same-key duplication problem is exactly the TODO called out in `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` ("We want to block while building the index and return the same index for the key … simple mutex not great … we don't want to block while anything in building, just the same key"). A per-key lock (e.g. a `sync.Map` of in-progress builds, or a sharded mutex keyed by `NamespacedResource`) is needed to actually fix the duplicate-build race while keeping different-key concurrency.

findings.title: Eager Init inside NewResourceServer changes the constructor's contract
findings.body:
`NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously before returning. The constructor will now block for the full duration of search-index build (potentially many seconds for large installations) and return an error if init fails. Previously the same errors would surface on the first RPC and the constructor returned quickly.
This breaks any caller that expected the constructor to be cheap (tests, callers that wire up dependencies lazily, callers that want to surface a degraded server, callers that explicitly rely on `server.Init` being invoked separately). The PR description itself flags this concern ("Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?") without answering it. Verify all callers of `NewResourceServer` and the SQL `NewBackend` (which now also returns only after `Init` succeeds, since its backend implements the resource LifecycleHooks path) before merging — at minimum, document the contract change on the function and make sure module startup won't now fail outright where it previously degraded.
